title: Worksheet 6: Two-Factor Authentication
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: Two-factor authentication, often abbreviated as 2FA, is a security process that requires a person to provide two different forms of proof before being allowed to access an account, rather than relying on just a single password. The idea behind two-factor authentication is that even if an attacker manages to steal or guess a person's password, they still cannot access the account without also having the second form of proof. The two factors typically come from different categories: something the person knows, such as a password or PIN, and something the person has, such as a code sent to their phone, a code generated by an authentication app, or a physical security key. Some systems also use a third category, something the person is, such as a fingerprint or face scan, which is known as biometric authentication. Because two-factor authentication adds an extra barrier for attackers to get past, security experts widely recommend enabling it on important accounts, such as email and banking, whenever it is available.

questions.text: Two-factor authentication is best described as:
questions.correct: A process requiring two different forms of proof before accessing an account

questions.text: According to the paragraph, what is the benefit of two-factor authentication if an attacker steals a password?
questions.correct: The attacker still cannot access the account without the second form of proof
distractors: The attacker gains full access anyway

questions.text: According to the paragraph, "something the person has" could include:
questions.correct: A code sent to their phone or a physical security key

questions.text: What is biometric authentication, according to the paragraph?
questions.correct: Using something the person is, such as a fingerprint or face scan

questions.text: According to the paragraph, what do security experts recommend?
questions.correct: Enabling two-factor authentication on important accounts whenever available
